counterevidence.summary: No runtime caller-controlled file or URL reaches this path; external producer and network changes are blocked; protected main and manual deployment reduce likelihood.

dataflow.summary: Alter vendored bytes -> recompute embedded pins -> recompute registry importedSha256 -> normal validation and build accept -> Pages publishes altered provenance-labelled result.

reachability.summary: Reachable only through a committed repository data mutation followed by review/merge, normal CI/build and Pages deployment.

confidence.rationale: Static dataflow and a dynamic same-count co-digested mutation both reproduced acceptance on the exact scanned commit.

findings.remediation: Add separately code-reviewed imported SHA-256 values for every admitted source to executable release policy; require the registry digest to match before trusting bytes; directly require the reviewed federation-lock byte pin in its standalone builder; add a same-count co-digested source-and-registry mutation regression test.
remediationTests: Normal production source validation passes exact pins
Same-count source and registry co-mutation fails before content consumption
Federated builder rejects any federation lock whose raw bytes differ from the reviewed pin

rootCause.summary: The code-reviewed release policy binds source identifiers, paths and counts, while the expected byte digest is read from source-locks.json alongside the data it is meant to authenticate. The independent federation-lock byte pin is not exercised by normal build admission.

severity.rationale: Successful exploitation can publish forged source-derived records under the project's provenance claims, but requires merged repository write authority and cannot be triggered by a page visitor or upstream network attacker.

findings.summary: The normal source admission path validates imported source bytes against a digest supplied by the same mutable registry. A repository-level change can therefore replace same-count source data, recompute all nested and registry digests, and publish altered records under checksum-bound provenance claims without changing a separately admitted release identity.
findings.title: Normal build accepts co-digested source-lock substitution

validation.summary: A same-count federation-lock mutation with recomputed entry, aggregate and lock digests was accepted by the production semantic validator; code inspection confirms normal source admission trusts the registry's co-mutable digest.
